content.text: Croyden buries the ransom at Greenberry Point, then returns to town. He and Macloud leave Annapolis, catch a boat at Baltimore, arrive in Hampton, stop at Ashburton, and continue to Clarendon. Elaine enters Clarendon, reunites with Croyden, and explains her release. Macloud and Davila join them. A memorandum reveals that Parmenter’s jewels are hidden in the southeast corner of the front cellar at the Hampton house. The group descends to the cellar, excavates the iron box, carries it to the library, and discovers magnificent jewels, including necklaces presented to Elaine and Davila. The remainder is an extensive antiquarian survey of British gardening, orchards, horticultural writers, landscape designers, botanists, poets, and their books, portraits, theories, and devotion to rural beauty.
